as_written_in_papers.quote: A heterozygous c.1449 C > G (NM_022162) mutation on exon 4 in the NOD/NACHT domain of NOD2 on chromosome 16 was identified.
Analysis of the protein variant revealed that the mutation was C483W (p.Cys483Trp).

cases.statement: Two carriers in one family: the affected proband (a 9-year-old girl) and her asymptomatic father. The father has no pipeline identity in the batch.

people.label: proband
people.key_phenotypes: symmetric boggy polyarthritis of wrists and ankles from age 3 (non-erosive); brownish annular infiltrative skin plaques; noncaseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells on skin biopsy; no uveitis; no camptodactyly

quotes.quote: A 9-years-old girl was referred to our pediatric rheumatology clinic due to large lumps over bilateral dorsal wrists and ankles since the age of 3 (Fig. 1A and B).
No range of motion limitation, camptodactyly or dactylitis was noted during physical examination.
Despite the chronicity and extravagance of her joint inflammation, the arthritis was non-erosive.
Multiple brownish annular infiltrative plaques without pruritus or pain was noted months before her initial visit to our clinic (Fig. 1D and E).
No uveitis or intraocular inflammation were recognized during ophthalmic examination.
A heterozygous c.1449 C > G (NM_022162) mutation on exon 4 in the NOD/NACHT domain of NOD2 on chromosome 16 was identified.

people.label: father
people.identity: no identity in batch (asymptomatic carrier relative)
people.key_phenotypes: asymptomatic; lacks clinical Blau/EOS phenotype per the authors

quotes.quote: A novel C483W NOD2 mutation was identify in the proband and her asymptomatic father.
the fact that proband’s father harbors the same C483W NOD2 mutation but lacks clinical BS/EOS phenotype itself suggests that this NOD2 mutation was incompletely penetrated.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The proband has arthritis, skin granulomatous plaques and biopsy-proven noncaseating granulomas but no uveitis; the authors diagnosed EOS/BS despite absent uveitis. Infection and other causes were tested: ANCA, ANA, RF, HLA-B27, chest radiograph and QuantiFERON-TB were negative, and special stains showed no microorganisms. Whole exome sequencing was done; results for other genes are not reported.

quotes.quote: Skin biopsy from the indurated brownish plaques over her right pre-tibial region revealed small noncaseating granulomas inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and neutrophils infiltration in dermis and subcutis, consistent with sarcoidosis (Fig. 2A and B).
Levels of complements C3, C4 and tests for antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, ANCA and HLA-B27 genotype were all negative.
Chest radiography study and QuantiFERON-TB Gold test for the survey of intra-thoracic lesions and mycobacterium infection revealed negative results.
Negative findings under acid fast stain, Fite’s stain and Periodic acid–Schiff stain suggested absent of microorganisms and negative polysaccharides accumulation (Fig. 2C and D).
the patient was diagnosed with EOS/BS despite the absence of uveitis during the follow up period.
In suspect of Blau syndrome, genomic DNA was extracted from patient’s peripheral blood cells and whole exome sequencing including exon–intron boundaries was performed.

segregation.statement: One unaffected carrier (the father) and one non-carrier parent (the mother); one affected carrier (the proband). Older relatives were not available for segregation study.

quotes.quote: The electropherogram shows the sequence of heterozygous c.1449 C > G transition on exon 4 in the NOD/NACHT domain of NOD2 in the patient and her father (orange arrows).
Such mutation was not found in her mother (blue arrow)
Due to the shortage of genetic material from elder family members of the proband, we were unable to confirmed the pattern of penetrance via classical segregation study.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: both parents were Sanger-tested and the variant was inherited from the father; the mother does not carry it. Parentage testing is not reported.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing of the proband and her parents were further arranged with a result showing that the proband’s mutant was inherited from her father (Fig. 3A and B).

functional.statement: Two assays. (1) Construct: HEK293T overexpression with an NF-κB luciferase reporter, R334W as positive and R311W as negative control; the authors state C483W is gain-of-function (numeric values are in a figure only). (2) Patient cells: p-NFκB staining of CD11b+ PBMCs without MDP was 20.5% in the proband, 10.9% in the carrier father, 0.9% in the mother, 5.1% in healthy controls (n = 3) and 28.1% in an R334W patient; plasma IL-6 and TNF-α were raised in the proband and the R334W control.

quotes.quote: We used R334W mutation of NOD2 as a positive control and R311W SNP as a negative control.
The results supported that the C483W mutation was confirmed to be a gain-of-function mutation.
The p-NFκB^+/CD11b^+ cells account for 20.5%, 10.9%, 0.9%, 5.1% and 28.1% of all CD11b^+ cells in the proband, her father, mother, healthy controls and the BS/EOS control, respectively.
Moreover, likely result from NFκB autoactivation, the level of plasma cytokines IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) were also elevated in the proband and the BS/EOS (R334W) control (Fig. 3E).

Specifically, the percentage of p-NFκB^+/CD11b^+ cells and the plasma level of proinflammatory cytokines seem to be lower in proband’s father as compared to the proband and the positive BS control (Fig. 3C, D and E).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (Cys456Trp on NP_001357395.1; stated as C483W on NM_022162 numbering). The authors describe Blau-associated NOD2 changes as gain-of-function and place C483W in HD1 of the NOD/NACHT domain among other Blau-associated variants.

quotes.quote: Blau syndrome (BS) is a rare autoinflammatory disorder with NOD2 gain-of-function mutation and characterized by autoactivation of the NFκB pathway.
The C483W mutation discovered in our proband and her father, is located on the HD1 within the NOD/NACHT domain, clustered with the BS/EOS associated variants.

computational_predictions.statement: As reported: SIFT 0.912, PolyPhen2 1, CADD 24, DANN 0.994, all described by the authors as damaging.

quotes.quote: The functional prediction scores: SIFT = 0.912, PolyPhen2 = 1, CADD = 24 and DANN = 0.994 all asserted the variant as damaging.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Allele frequency 0 in gnomAD and in Taiwan Biobank whole-genome data from 1,475 unrelated healthy individuals; not found in published articles or Infevers.

quotes.quote: The allelic frequency was 0 in both the Genome Aggregation Database (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/) and the genotype data from the Taiwan Biobank (https://taiwanview.twbiobank.org.tw/) comprised of whole genome sequencing result from 1,475 unrelated healthy individuals in Taiwan.

No data on the C483W NOD2 variant was found in published articles or the Infevers database (an online database for autoinflammatory mutations, available at https://infevers.umai-montpellier.fr/) [13, 14].

authors_classification.statement: No ACMG classification. The authors state their data support pathogenicity of C483W for BS/EOS with incomplete penetrance.

quotes.quote: Through genetic testing and functional exams, our data supported the pathogenicity of C483W NOD2 mutation underlining BS/EOS with incomplete penetrance.
In conclusions, we’ve demonstrated that C483W NOD2 mutation is a novel mutation underlining BS/EOS with incomplete penetrance.

concerns: Numbering: the paper uses NM_022162; the batch's NM_001370466.1 numbers are 81 nt / 27 codons lower (c.1449 -> c.1368; C483 -> C456). The stated c.1449C>G and C483W are consistent with each other on the paper's numbering.
Non-penetrance: the father carries the variant and is asymptomatic; his p-NFκB value (10.9%) lies between the healthy controls (5.1%) and the proband (20.5%).
The proband lacks uveitis and camptodactyly; the diagnosis rests on arthritis, skin granulomas and the functional data.
Whole exome sequencing was performed, but the paper does not report results for other genes.
The reported SIFT value (0.912) is described as damaging; the panel may wish to check the score direction the authors used.
Healthy controls in the p-NFκB assay were n = 3; luciferase values are in a figure, not in the text.
notes_for_panel: Single family (PMID 36192768): affected proband, asymptomatic carrier father, non-carrier mother. Construct and patient-cell assays both reported, with positive and negative controls for the construct assay.
